issue.title: Redline's reply says only the standfirst explained the case study's trial, where the headline names it too, and the reply checker passes it

labels.name: needs-info
labels.description: Waiting on reporter for more information

issue.body:
*This was generated by AI while building #477.*

Measured while building #477 and filed from its exit, which files every miss of the candidate reading that ships.

## What was measured

A statement of Redline's reply about the text as it arrived that the text contradicts, read by the reply checker and not named, then reworded after the check and delivered — with the #477 candidate in place.

- **Run:** `post-case-study-clean-file-3` in `docs/evaluation/editorial-477/runs/` (on the branch `kntnt-orchestrate/main/477` until it is integrated), `case-study-clean` delivered to `output.md`, `claude-opus-5-5` at high deliberation.
- **The draft the checker read**, finding 2: *”Försöket” fick sin referent bara från ingressen.* The closing paragraph: *Hänvisningar som bara ingressen förklarade, eller som inget förklarade, gjordes tydliga i ingressen och inledningen.*
- **The delivered reply**, finding 2: *Det var bara ingressen som förklarade vad ”Försöket” syftade på.* The closing paragraph is delivered in the draft's words.
- **The text as received:** the headline *Gemensam ärendebild hjälper, säger Elm Quay om loggförsöket* names the trial too, so the standfirst was not the only place that said what *Försöket* referred to.
- **Judges:** reply judge A records both statements as false; reply judge B and both correction judges do not. The #477 plan puts a miss in a run on one judge.

## Why it is filed

The finding's sentence counts as #477's target only because it was reworded after the check; the falsehood itself was in the draft and the checker passed it. The closing paragraph's sentence is the same claim, unchanged since the draft. Both are a checker miss of a statement about the text as received, which #477 does not own. `results.md` in the same directory records it.

comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Diagnose and repair the reply check's missed whole-text exclusivity claim about the received article.

## What to build

Make the first list of Redline's reply checker test claims about the received text against that complete text, with the scope the reply actually asserts. In particular, do not pass an unqualified statement that only the standfirst explains a referent without checking the headline and other passages too. Keep a body-only observation separate: a body may still need to stand without the standfirst, even when a headline names the subject. Do not turn this into permission to reject useful body orientation or to treat every heading as a complete explanation.

**Verification and redundancy check:** Read `case-study-clean` and #477's `post-case-study-clean-file-3` draft, checker return and final reply. The received headline names `loggförsöket`; the draft says the standfirst alone supplied the trial's referent, and that assertion survives the check. The checker instead faults the summary's claim of additional changes. The reply judge A counts two false statements; judge B and both transition judges do not, so this is a preserved split under the plan's one-judge-miss rule, not consensus. The current shared delivery contract already requires universal claims to be checked against every part they cover, and the checker lists them; this issue concerns a residual false negative, not an absent generic rule. No fresh native run was launched in triage. No `.out-of-scope/` KB exists. The #478 decision declined widening the second list's attribution accounting and does not reject this first-list problem.

**Key interfaces:** The reply check's received/delivered text inputs and first-list factual tests; Redline's application of a returned correction. #489 owns newly introduced post-check falsehoods; here the target statement is already false or overbroad in the checked draft. Whether the underlying lead rewrite was licensed belongs to #491.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Commit a frozen plan before native runs, using #477's staged arms, complete reply states, independent neutral-path judging and disclosed split rule. Use a fresh pre-change arm on one provider-native seat, with `case-study-clean` as three response/file-target pairs per arm. Judge the drafted statement, checker return and terminal statement separately.
- [ ] Before candidate wording, freeze and independently validate checker contrasts that distinguish an unqualified whole-text `only/nowhere` assertion contradicted by paratext, an accurately limited body-only assertion, and a true whole-text exclusivity assertion. Validation must test the actual semantic distinction, including `names` versus `explains`, without candidate hints.
- [ ] Replay the historical saved checker input and the validated contrasts three times per arm as isolated checker probes. Record those probes separately: they can diagnose what the checker sees but cannot establish native Redline reproduction or substitute for the fresh baseline.
- [ ] A native target miss is a false whole-text assertion already in the draft that the checker fails to name and the terminal reply still carries. Use the frozen one-judge-miss rule inherited from #477 and preserve every split; do not classify a valid body-only statement as false merely because a heading names the subject.
- [ ] If the fresh native baseline reproduces, try the smallest motivated first-list correction. The target is that the checker names the overbroad statement with the correct text and contradicting passage, and the final reply removes or accurately narrows it. True exclusivity and properly scoped body-only contrasts are not falsely flagged; the Text Artifact is unchanged by the reply check.
- [ ] If native reproduction is absent, ship no speculative checker wording and record that outcome, keeping any replay improvement separate. Otherwise use only the protocol's bounded revise/ship rule and file remaining misses. Do not build #489's application fix, #491's article review fix, or the second-list widening declined in #478 here.
- [ ] Preserve the one-shot checker, final Proofread pass, source/destination/cleanup contracts, and unmentioned checked sentences verbatim. Regenerate the catalog after shipped-file changes and pass the four project checks in CONTRIBUTING.md.

**Out of scope:** Removing the independent-body requirement, deciding all lead referents by the headline alone, changing the clean corpus to fit a reviewer, and adding a second checker pass.

Verifier verdict:

# FAIL — ticket #490

Verified independently in `/Users/thomas/Projects/skills/.git/kntnt-orchestrate/490` at unchanged HEAD `7b0ae5a2ef7f14d5b3be424e462d246407640e78`. The actual evaluation start is `4cf05813f94c2fa7147898878027835e14d29859`. No implementation-role commit exists. The ticket's required evaluation is incomplete, and its project gate fails deterministically. This is neither a reproduced nor a not-reproduced result.

## Project gate executed independently

I ran the four exact supplied commands sequentially. Their complete command strings, process identities, outputs and exit receipts are preserved beside this verdict as `gate-1` through `gate-4` files.

| Command | Independent result |
| --- | --- |
| `uvx ruff check .` | Exit 0: `All checks passed!` |
| `uvx ruff format --check .` | Exit 0: `8498 files already formatted` |
| The exact supplied `uvx --with … mypy` command, all 90 supplied source files | Exit 0: `Success: no issues found in 90 source files` |
| `uv run --with pytest --with pytest-xdist --with pyyaml pytest -n auto` | Exit 1: `1 failed, 2734 passed in 167.55s (0:02:47)` |

The failing test is `tests/test_adr.py::test_every_cited_number_has_a_record`. Its evidence is:

```text
{'0241': ['docs/evaluation/editorial-490/plan.md']}
```

`docs/evaluation/editorial-490/plan.md:46` prospectively names `ADR-0241`; no record carries that number. The protocol explicitly requires decision-record citations in committed evidence to resolve, while separately forbidding editing a frozen plan after runs start. A future conditional record is not an existing record.

Defect Class: Decision-record citations in committed evaluation evidence must resolve, including citations in prospective branches that were not taken.

The failure is a strict subset of the suite. I reran exactly that failing test in isolation three times on the same unchanged HEAD, using the exact narrowed command:

```sh
uv run --with pytest --with pytest-xdist --with pyyaml pytest -n auto tests/test_adr.py::test_every_cited_number_has_a_record
```

| Isolated rerun | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Exit 1; same missing `0241`; `1 failed in 2.32s` |
| 2 | Exit 1; same missing `0241`; `1 failed in 1.29s` |
| 3 | Exit 1; same missing `0241`; `1 failed in 7.25s` |

All three failed, so this is deterministic under the supplied protocol. No complete rerun is authorized by the all-three-green flake branch and none was made. The original run used 14 xdist workers on Darwin, Python 3.14.8. At `2026-10-02T20:28:12.564622+02:00`, recorded load averages were `9.4921875`, `6.64208984375`, `6.013671875`. Complete logs, the load snapshot and each isolated exit are preserved; load does not excuse this repeatedly isolated reference failure.

## Every acceptance criterion

1. **Unmet — frozen plan and fresh native baseline.** Commit `41773ae9f652a35918f1debd474e3eb401c9a229` froze the plan, contrasts and briefs at 20:09:36, before the first native validator at 20:11:35. `55c7ace2` corrected a harness filename before that launch; the plan, inputs, expectations and briefs remain unchanged after the freeze. The plan specifies immutable arms, three response/file pairs, complete reply states, independent neutral readers and the one-judge-miss rule. However, all six required fresh pre-change Redline rows are explicitly skipped in `docs/evaluation/records/redline-gpt-2026-10-02-490.md`. No fresh native drafted statement, checker return or terminal statement was produced or separately judged. Ten contrast-validator sessions are not native Redline baseline runs.

   Defect Class: Mandatory fresh native baseline rows and their complete state judgements cannot be replaced by historical states, contrast validation or skipped-row records.

2. **Unmet as the frozen validation prerequisite — the intended control set did not validate.** I read every frozen pair, its intended reading, both independent validation reports, the supplied briefs, native turn contexts and tool calls, and staging inventories. The ten actual validators used fresh `gpt-6.1-sol` / `xhigh` sessions and neutral physical paths. Their material consisted of `text.md` and `reply.md` plus harness dispatch material; the supplied brief carried no expected verdict or candidate wording. Both readers found q1 false because its headline explicitly identifies what was tried; q2 true within its body-opening scope; q4's naming and complete-explanation statements true; and q5 false because its subheading states the supposedly absent proposition. This exercises the semantic distinction rather than matching the word `only`.

   But q3 was prospectively assigned the true whole-text exclusivity role and both readers found it false. Its body says `Försöket pågick i åtta veckor`, referring in context to the same repair-log trial. Both explain why this communicates that the trial happened outside the standfirst, even without repeating the organisation's name. These findings are preserved accurately. q4 supplies a valid, more fully specified exclusivity proposition, but the frozen method at `plan.md:19` requires support for each intended contrast and explicitly stops dependent work when a contrast is invalid. The planned prerequisite therefore remains failed. Stopping instead of relabelling q3 was faithful to the plan; it does not finish the ticket.

   Defect Class: A frozen semantic control set whose intended reading fails independent validation cannot authorize the dependent measurement or be treated as a successfully validated set.

3. **Unmet — isolated checker probes.** The protocol record explicitly skips all eighteen pre-change probes: three historical-input replays and three repeats of each of q1 through q5. The eighteen conditional candidate probes are also skipped. There is no checker probe return or independent probe judgement. The historical input was preserved, and its separation from native reproduction is correct, but preserving input is not replaying it.

   Defect Class: Required repeated isolated checker exercises need actual checker returns and recorded judgements; scheduled or skipped rows provide no behavioural result.

4. **Met as the required definition and scope rule; native exercise remains missing under criterion 1.** `plan.md:32` defines T1 as a false whole-text statement already in the draft, missed by the checker and retained terminally. `plan.md:40` preserves the one-judge-miss rule and every contrary reading. The state-judge brief separately tests draft, checker and terminal statements, respects limited body scope and distinguishes naming from explaining. The actual q2 validators preserve the valid body-only observation; q4 validators do not treat a heading naming a subject as the complete explanation. I also read #477's original saved draft, checker and terminal states and its reply/transition readings: reply judge A counts two false exclusivity statements, while reply judge B and both transition judges do not. That split is preserved, not rewritten as consensus or promoted into fresh reproduction. There is no incorrect new native classification because no native Redline run occurred.

5. **Unmet pending its mandatory measurement prerequisite — conditional first-list repair and controls.** No fresh native baseline established whether the correction branch should run. No candidate exists, so there is no exercised evidence that the first list names the overbroad statement with the correct text and contradicting passage, that the terminal reply removes or narrows it, that true/body-only controls stay unflagged, or that the Text Artifact stays byte-identical across that check. The restraint against choosing speculative wording was respected. This is an unresolved conditional disposition, not evidence that a repair works or that the no-repair branch applies.

   Defect Class: Conditional product acceptance requires an observed prerequisite and the corresponding measured branch; an unexecuted prerequisite establishes neither branch.

6. **Unmet as a completed disposition; its scope and restraint requirements were respected.** `results.md` and the record correctly call the evaluation incomplete and expressly refuse a not-reproduced conclusion. No speculative wording, replay improvement, candidate/revise cycle or new product-defect result was shipped. No #489 application fix, #491 article-review fix or #478 second-list widening was built. However, no complete baseline establishes absence or presence of native reproduction, so neither the requested not-reproduced outcome nor the conditional bounded repair/ship outcome exists.

   Defect Class: An incomplete evaluation cannot satisfy a measured reproduced/not-reproduced disposition, even when its stop boundary and lack of product changes are recorded honestly.

7. **Unmet — required project gate.** The product contracts are preserved: the ticket's three commits changed no shipped file, tests, corpus or CONTRIBUTING file relative to `4cf05813`. The current reply-check still requires one fresh check, correction only of returned items, unmentioned sentences word for word, no Text Artifact change and no second check; Redline still invokes final Proofread once and retains its delivery/source/cleanup contract. Catalog regeneration was unnecessary because no shipped file changed, and the catalog is unchanged. Nevertheless, the four required project checks have not all passed: the independently repeated ADR reference failure above prevents acceptance.

   Defect Class: Required whole-project verification remains failed when committed ticket evidence introduces an unresolved invariant, regardless of whether shipped product files changed.

## Scope and integrity review

The ticket-owned delta from its actual starting revision is confined to the #490 evaluation packet, its protocol-format record and its `.kntnt-orchestrate/490.md` delivery fragment. The other changes visible from the older issue-body revision were already present at the actual ticket start and are not attributed to this ticket. No test was weakened, removed or skipped to obtain green results. Neither the supplied current gate nor the supplied base gate is narrowed; their command lists are identical, and CONTRIBUTING is unchanged in this ticket. No clean corpus rewrite or second checker pass was introduced. Frozen evidence was not edited after validation began. No role-specific commit-role declaration exists; the packet identifies the starting product SHA and correctly says no implementation-role commit exists. There is no push/PR/release delivery clause to score.

The invalid-control stop is recorded candidly and is supported by the saved native exercises. It is a useful unfinished result, not completion of the whole ticket. I did not start any additional native product trial or derive any additional project gate.

Orchestrate parks #490 at a concrete method/record boundary under `--yes`. The ordinary task of authoring a valid true-exclusivity contrast is already authorized by the latest Agent Brief; validation or behavioral criteria are not waived.

The Agent Brief requires: “Before candidate wording, freeze and independently validate checker contrasts” and a fresh native baseline. The existing q3 intended-true control was false for both independent readers, so its frozen plan stopped the dependent measurement. All native baseline and probe rows remain unrun. The original freeze, ten validations and first record are preserved; amend 1 added a full audit at `d199b3bb`, with no native product run, implementation or new quality verdict. The unresolved reserved-ADR citation remains a gate failure.

The authoritative evaluation protocol says “A re-run is a new record, and the earlier one stays” and requires `<skill>-<provider-family>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<issue>.md`, with one record per evaluation. `docs/evaluation/records/redline-gpt-2026-10-02-490.md` is already occupied by the stopped campaign. Historical suffix formats predate the current naming rule and do not settle a new same-day format.

**Maintainer decision:** What is the recording boundary for a new prospective validation design followed by this ticket's first native baseline: an additive continuation of the existing evaluation/record, retaining all earlier entries and frozen evidence, or a separate evaluation? If separate, state an authorized issue-qualified record identity for the same provider family and date. Specify how the new prospective phase may supersede the failed prerequisite without editing, relabelling or discarding its original evidence. This asks for the method/record boundary; it does not ask permission to construct the contrast already required by the ticket, or to reinterpret q3 as true.

The ticket must state that boundary before the stopped measurement continues. No amendment quality outcome or terminal Ticket Resolution is recorded for this decision. Lifetime `amends_spent=1`, phase `building`; the path is not exhausted and attempt 2 has not been spent.

## New prospective current-resolution campaign, 2026-10-03

The user's new instruction authorizes autonomous technical repair and the accepted #499 capture/two-stage preparation method. Root has allocated current completion of #490 to the Redline owner in the ordinary editorial-repair branch. #499 is a native blocked-by prerequisite. This is a separate fresh Oct3 campaign/packet and an issue-qualified new record where the corpus protocol governs; focused regression packets follow the staging rules they actually use. It preserves every Oct2 plan, input, actual completed/unjudgeable/unrun row, judgement, sealed-state gap, gate outcome, parked workflow phase and lifetime amend count unchanged. Prepare a NEW genuine whole-text exclusivity control; the old rejected q3 stays rejected. Validation distinguishes names from explains and correctly limited body-only from unqualified whole-text assertions. Isolated probes diagnose but do not establish native Redline reproduction. First-list semantic candidate requires its own native false draft passed through to terminal; no second-list expansion.

Non-reproduction ships no speculative wording. New/current histories remain separately identifiable, all actual remaining misses retained; independent whole-current-method review, catalog when due and four CONTRIBUTING checks precede root's integration/reconciliation.
